cim_eredeti: Looking at the future of artificial intelligence in the workplace
szoveg_eredeti:

AI could impact every career industry to some degree.

Technology is something that people may use every day. However, some may have concerns about artificial intelligence in the work industry.

Learning Technology Specialist Heather Thach with the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga believes that AI could impact every career industry to some degree.

AI has been around since the 1950s, but Thach says it has become more prevalent since 2022.

Thach says that when most people think of AI, they think of generative AI.

“Those early models that we saw come out... we are already pretty revolutionary in what they allow users to do,” Thach said.

One example of this kind of generative AI is ChatGPT, which is one of the most common platforms of AI. Users can ask the tech to edit photos, organize research, or get inspiration.

Thach encourages UTC staff to familiarize themselves with AI.

“One of the things I talk to faculty about, with the perspective of generative AI, is understanding what students in their field will be expected to do once they go out onto the job market,” Thach said.

Advancements in technology may bring a level of uncertainty.

A recent UTC data center panel got experts talking about the future of AI in the workplace.

“It's going to become a skill that's needed in the workforce, and it really already is a skill because AI has been around for a while,” says one panelist.

Another adds, “But what they've done, and they haven't done enough to kind of…they've instilled fear, maybe; not done enough to calm down fears.”

Thach believes everyone is entitled to their own opinions about AI, but she serves as a guide for UTC staff on navigating a new era of future workers.

Before going into any job, Thach encourages future employees to ask if and how AI can or will be used.

“Be able to anticipate what it's going to give you and anticipate any limitations as well,” she said.

Regardless, Thach says it's important that we continue to learn, as AI is constantly changing.

“I think a degree of literacy is going to be required,” she said. “If you are asked to use it in a certain way, you need to know how it's going to work.”
